name: Jena Griswold

summary.text: Jena Griswold is Colorado's Secretary of State, first elected in 2018 and reelected in 2022; she grew up in a working-class family in Estes Park, Colorado.
She is the Democratic nominee for Colorado attorney general in the November 2026 general election, having defeated three rivals in the June 30 primary.

experience.text: Colorado Secretary of State, 2019–present (elected 2018, reelected 2022, defeating Republican Pam Anderson 55%-42%).
Law degree from the University of Pennsylvania Law School; practiced international anti-corruption law in Washington, D.C., then served as Director of the Colorado Governor's Washington, D.C. office.

record.title: Petition to bar Tina Peters from administering Mesa County's 2022 elections
record.detail: As Secretary of State, she was a petitioner in a Mesa County District Court case seeking to keep Clerk Tina Peters from serving as designated election official for the 2022 elections. On May 10, 2022 the court enjoined Peters and Deputy Clerk Belinda Knisley from that role and confirmed Brandi Bantz as designated election official for the 2022 election cycle.

record.title: Named respondent in Trump v. Anderson ballot-eligibility case
record.detail: Six voters sued in her official capacity as Secretary of State to keep Donald Trump off Colorado's 2024 Republican primary ballot over the Jan. 6 Capitol attack; the Colorado Supreme Court later ruled 4-3 that Trump was disqualified, before the U.S. Supreme Court reversed.

record.title: Election-security legislation backed as Secretary of State
record.detail: Her campaign says she 'spearheaded legislation to keep Colorado elections safe,' including criminalizing threats to election workers, making it illegal to bring guns near voting centers, and making it a felony to compromise voting equipment (exact bill and date not given on the fetched page; bounded to the start of her tenure).

record.title: Impeachment resolution against Griswold failed in House Judiciary Committee
record.detail: A Republican-sponsored resolution to impeach Griswold, citing her comments ahead of the Trump v. Anderson Supreme Court case, failed in the Colorado House Judiciary Committee on April 9, 2024, after being introduced April 4, 2024.

record.title: Declined U.S. Department of Justice request for unredacted voter registration list
record.detail: As Secretary of State, her office said it would not hand over Coloradans' sensitive voting information in response to a U.S. Department of Justice request for the unredacted statewide voter registration list. The department announced a lawsuit against her over the request on Dec. 11, 2025.

positions.source_title: Griswold, Allen vie to become next attorney general
positions.quote: I will always fight to make sure that all Coloradans have access to reproductive healthcare, including birth control, IVF, and abortion access.
positions.note: From Griswold's answer in a Colorado Politics candidate questionnaire.

positions.source_title: Michael Allen, Jena Griswold: Colorado attorney general election voter guide
positions.quote: These lawsuits are critical to protect our state and stand up to Trump. I will continue to join or file lawsuits when Trump is breaking the law and it affects Colorado.
positions.note: From a Colorado Sun candidate interview on whether she agrees with AG Weiser's more than 80 lawsuits against the Trump administration; she said she agrees with the approach.

positions.source_title: Griswold, Allen vie to become next attorney general
positions.quote: Trump has carried out a campaign of retribution against Colorado because of Tina Peters and our gold standard elections.
positions.note: Describes Colorado's current election system, which she administers, as 'gold standard.'

positions.source_title: Michael Allen, Jena Griswold: Colorado attorney general election voter guide
positions.quote: It is not our job to enforce the law of the federal government.
positions.note: Said directly in response to a question about the ballot measure requiring law enforcement to assist ICE in certain cases, though as Secretary of State she said she does not take an official position on ballot measures she oversees. The preceding sentence in the same answer was: 'Local officials, state officials, are not federal immigration agents.'

positions.source_title: Michael Allen, Jena Griswold: Colorado attorney general election voter guide
positions.quote: I will prosecute ICE agents who commit crimes, and if there is a case to stop their inhumane immigration policies.
positions.note: Called current federal immigration enforcement under ICE 'terrorizing' in the same answer.

positions.source_title: In shift, Sen. Bennet supports Colorado constitutional amendment for emergency redistricting
positions.quote: Colorado Secretary of State Jena Griswold, who is running for attorney general in 2026, has also supported a ballot initiative to allow for emergency redistricting.
positions.note: The article reports she supported a proposed initiative to allow emergency mid-decade redistricting, which is the opposite of the statement (Amendment 86 makes off-cycle redistricting harder). Coded disagree. Corrected in build review on 2026-10-14; the first pass had coded it as agree.

positions.source_title: About — Jena Griswold for Attorney General
positions.quote: made it illegal to bring guns near voting centers
positions.note: Describes a narrow gun restriction (near polling places) she championed as Secretary of State, not a broad gun-control position.

positions.source_title: Michael Allen, Jena Griswold: Colorado attorney general election voter guide
positions.quote: Addressing corporate polluters and protecting our climate has to be the top priority of the next AG and it will absolutely be mine
positions.note: Says addressing corporate polluters and protecting the climate will be her top priority as attorney general; support for speeding the shift to renewable energy is inferred from that.

research_notes: A Colorado Sun / Noticias Univision debate between Griswold and Allen was scheduled for 6:30pm MDT on Oct. 14, 2026 (the day this research was done); no recap or transcript was available yet at research time, so it is not reflected here — worth checking for a post-debate article before publishing. Amendment 81 is called 'Proposition 81' in a September 2026 Colorado Politics article and 'Amendment 81' in October 2026 pieces; this may reflect its reclassification before certification — worth double-checking the final ballot designation. Could not source Griswold positions on fentanyl penalties (Prop 132), child trafficking sentencing (Prop 133), hunting rights (Amendment 83), transgender-related measures (Props 134/135), mail-ballot ID (Amendment 84), plain-language ballots (Amendment 85), or federal tax/tariff/public-lands questions despite searching; left as unknown rather than inferred from party. The jenaforcolorado.com campaign site is a single-page JavaScript app, so only the 'About' and 'Issues' landing text could be retrieved (no dated sub-pages). Second pass 2026-10-14: checked the Denver Post's Oct. 3, 2026 AG candidate Q&A and Robert Tann's Oct. 14, 2026 Denver Post recap of the Griswold-Allen debate; both reinforce her existing challenge-federal-policies and stricter-gun-laws positions (she said at the debate she wants a stricter assault weapons ban than SB25-003) but do not address fentanyl penalties, child-trafficking sentencing, or any other uncoded statement, so no new positions were added.
